texts.preamble: Saj Food Products Private Limited vs The State Of West Bengal & Ors on 31 January, 2025 Author: Amrita Sinha Bench: Amrita Sinha D/L 392 31.01.2025 Court No.14 Pradip In The High Court At Calcutta Constitutional Writ Jurisdiction Wpa 1887 of 2025 Saj Food Products Private Limited Vs. The State of West Bengal & Ors. Mr. Abhratosh Majumdar, Sr. Adv. Mr. Sayan Sinha Mr. Nilanjan Bhattacharya Mr. Adil Naser ... for the Petitioner. Mr. Niltpal Chatterjee Ms. Munmun Ganguly ... for the State. Mr. Dhiraj Trivedi, Dsgi Mr. Arijit Majumdar ...for the Union of India. 1 . The prohibition order under Section 36(3) (B) of The Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 dated 10th January, 2025 passed by the Designated Officer (FSSAI) and DFSIO, Murshidabad is impugned in the instant writ petition. 2.
texts.facts: 1 . The prohibition order under Section 36(3) (B) of The Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 dated 10th January, 2025 passed by the Designated Officer (FSSAI) and DFSIO, Murshidabad is impugned in the instant writ petition. 2. By the said order the petitioner has been directed to stop manufacturing of 'GOOGLY' biscuits, bearing Batch No. (FTWL17C) pkg-6th July, 2024. 3. For passing the said prohibition order, the Designated Officer relied upon the analysis report of the Food Analyst (Function) dated 18th November, 2024 mentioning that the sample does not Saj Food Products Private Limited vs The State Of West Bengal & Ors on 31 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/66244379/ 1 conform to the standard of biscuits as laid down in the Regulation No. 2.4.15.1 of FSS(FPS & FA) due to presence of non-permitted colour (tartrazine). The sample has been held to be 'unsafe'. 4. The petitioner challenges the jurisdiction of the Designated Officer in passing the order to stop manufacturing of the product. It has been submitted that, the said Officer does not have the authority to direct stoppage of manufacturing of the food product. It has also been submitted that, the authority which conducted the food analysis does not have the accreditation to test the quality of the food colour of a food product. 5. According to the petitioner, there is no appellate authority and as the prohibition order was passed by the Designated Officer, the appeal before the said authority will be illusory.
texts.arguments: 6. Learned counsel has referred to the report of food analysis by EFRAC in support of the submission that, tartrazine is a permitted food colour. 7. Prayer has been made to stay the operation of the impugned prohibition order.
